Swept 2026-08-16 with tools/check_api_arity.py, committed alongside this closure.

RESULT over the 460 method declarations in inc/Api.h:
  326  every shared parameter slot agrees
   38  C++ has extra trailing defaulted parameters, shared slots agree -- benign
        by design (the script simply does not expose an option)
    2  MISALIGNED
   94  no C++ declaration the tool could match, so NOT CHECKED

The two misalignments:
  inc-xkd  FindOpenAreas -- slot 2 is Flags to the script and regID to the C++.
           Live, and already filed.
  new      SetGlyphAt -- a 32-bit Glyph declared 16 bits wide in the API and
           cast down in the generated call. Not live; no script calls it.

WHAT THE DISCRIMINATOR TURNED OUT TO BE, because the first three attempts were
useless. Counting parameters flags 45 methods, nearly all benign: a C++ method
may carry trailing defaulted parameters the script does not expose, and
MoveDepth(NewDepth) against MoveDepth(NewDepth, safe=false) is correct. Comparing
parameter NAMES flags 61, nearly all pure renames -- 'fl' against 'flags', 'att'
against 'at'. What actually separates a defect from house style is the TYPE
CLASS of each slot: FindOpenAreas is dangerous because slot 2 is an integer to
the script and an rID to the C++, and the compiler cannot tell those apart
because rID is a uint32 underneath.

THE HONEST LIMIT: 94 of 460, about a fifth, were not checked because the tool
could not find a C++ declaration to compare against. That is a coverage gap, not
a clean bill of health. It is printed in the summary every run, and
'tools/check_api_arity.py --all' lists them.

Fixed and verified 2026-08-16.

THE FIX. Game::Play now writes logs/session.log on the first COMPLETED turn, unconditionally (src/Main.cpp, NoteGameplayReached). tools/headless.sh asks that file whether the session played, instead of asking logs/mapaudit.log. The marker sits beside the turn counter it describes, so no diagnostic switch can silence it.

VERIFIED, all three cases, same seed and key script:
  audit OFF, real play   exit 0, session.log written   (was exit 5, the bug)
  audit ON,  real play   exit 0, both logs written     (no regression)
  vacuous run            exit 5, no session.log        (still caught)

The vacuous run left 11 screens while correctly reporting no gameplay, which is why screens must never be used as the oracle -- that is recorded in the comment.

The harness also stopped reporting a missing audit log as 'never entered a map'. It now distinguishes: audit deliberately off, no gameplay, or armed-but-no-log (the switch did not take).

tools/check_headless.sh gains case 6, which fails if a session with the audit off is ever again called vacuous, or if the marker disappears.

tools/gate_compare.sh against the current baseline: 40 of 40 played, 6001 findings, 1 error line, no change, PASS.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: inc-2k3. A timing run must set INCURSION_MAP_AUDIT=0, and until now every such session discarded its own data.

Done 2026-08-16. build_macos.sh gains COMPILER=no, which builds a binary with no resource compiler, no parser and no preprocessor.

HOW, and it follows Windows rather than inventing anything. build.bat:93 already filters yygram.cpp, tokens.cpp and cpp*.c out of a Release build. The macOS script now does the same: with COMPILER=no it omits -DDEBUG and skips RComp, Art, yygram and Tokens, plus cpp1-6.c.

THE TRAP I HIT, recorded because the symptom is misleading: excluding all of src/*.c fails the link with four undefined symbols -- LZ_CompressFast, LZ_Uncompress, RLE_Compress, RLE_Uncompress. src/lz.c and src/rle.c are runtime compression that Registry needs to read a save or a module, not compiler support. Only cpp1-6.c may go.

honours OPT_DISALLOW (src/Player.cpp:683), the '(Debugging Commands)' entry

The object directory encodes COMPILER, so a shipping and a developer build can
never mix objects -- they differ by -DDEBUG, which changes real code.

Fixed 2026-08-16, by making a compiler-free build possible: COMPILER=no ./build_macos.sh. See inc-9df.3 for the mechanism.

PROVED, not asserted. src/Art.cpp is the GPLv2 ACCENT runtime and it defines exactly three functions: yyparse, yyselect, yymallocerror. All three are present in a default build and absent from a COMPILER=no build.

    nm ./incursion      | grep -c 'yyparse\|yyselect\|yymallocerror'   -> 3 present
    nm ./incursion-ship | grep -c 'yyparse\|yyselect\|yymallocerror'   -> 0

WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND MUST NOT BE FORGOTTEN: the DEFAULT build still contains
it, deliberately, because the developer binary is the only thing that can
produce mod/Incursion.Mod. That is fine -- a developer binary is never
distributed -- but it means the release pipeline MUST build with COMPILER=no.
Recorded as a requirement on inc-9df.4 rather than left as folklore.

NOT A LEGAL OPINION, and unchanged from the original filing: this is what the
source file states about itself. Anyone publishing a binary should confirm it
independently.

Fixed by tools/package_macos.sh: the packaging step copies libSDL2-2.0.0.dylib beside the binary and rewrites the load command to @executable_path. The reference is read out of the binary with otool rather than assuming a prefix, so an Intel Mac (/usr/local) packages correctly too. Static linking was rejected: it needs a custom SDL2 build and buys nothing here, since otool shows SDL2 pulls in no other Homebrew library, only system frameworks.

ONE THING THAT NEARLY SHIPPED A DEAD FOLDER. install_name_tool invalidates the signature the file already carried, and Apple Silicon refuses to run a Mach-O whose signature is present but broken. The script now re-signs both files ad-hoc immediately after the rewrite.

VERIFIED AS THE ISSUE ASKED, not by 'it runs here'. With /opt/homebrew/opt/sdl2 renamed away, and running from a temp directory outside the repo:
  CONTROL   repo ./incursion  -> dyld: Library not loaded: /opt/homebrew/opt/sdl2/lib/libSDL2-2.0.0.dylib
  TREATMENT packaged binary   -> no dyld error, 'Created renderer: metal', event loop running
The control failing is what gives the result meaning. The Homebrew symlink was restored afterwards and checked.

tools/check_package.sh gates this permanently: it rejects any absolute load path outside /usr/lib and /System/Library, and rejects a bundled dylib that is referenced but absent.
